To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the replication of a herpes simplex type-1 mutant virus, which is deficient in the immediate-early gene encoding Vmw110, is stimulated by human cytomegaovirus, but not by varicella-zooster virus, in low multiplicity of infection in human foetal-lung fibroblasts.

human cytomegalvirus (HCMC) is able to complement the defect of a herpes simplex type I (HSV-1), Vmw110 deletion, mutant (dl1403) when the viruses are co-infected at a low multiplicity of infection (m.o.i.).
human cytomegallovirus can compensate for a herpes simplex virus deletion in low multiplicity infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular biology of herpes simplex virus type-1 (HSV- 1).
the molecular biology of herpes simplex virus and the interaction between HSV-1 and HCMV.
the ability of HCMV to rescue a HSV-1 mutant in low multiplicity infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HCMV genome can complement the HSV-1 Vmw110 gene deletion in HFL cells, and the HCMV gene product responsible for this complementation has been mapped to the immediate-early region.

the ability of HCMV and possibly other human herpesvirues to complement the growth of dl1403 at low m.o.l. in HFL is not a result of a direct interaction between the two viruses but is a consequence of the induction of a cellular factor(s) which promotes the replication of dl1403.
